text: The chapter draws a 'decidability map' for first-order theories of algebraic structures. Which pairing is correct?
choices: The theory of abelian groups is decidable (Szmielew), while the full first-order theory of groups is undecidable (Tarski)
The theory of abelian groups is undecidable, while the full theory of groups is decidable
Both the theory of groups and the theory of abelian groups are undecidable
Th(ℝ; +, ·, ≤) is undecidable, while Th(ℤ; +, ·) is decidable
explanation: Szmielew (1955) proved the first-order theory of abelian groups decidable, whereas Tarski showed the full first-order theory of groups undecidable — commutativity marks the boundary. Option D reverses the real/integer situation: RCF = Th(ℝ;+,·,≤) is decidable (Tarski) while Th(ℤ;+,·) is undecidable.
